author: Codex root
scope: Mechanism design and hand derivation only; implementation and reproduction remain downstream.
name: L-F: reserve capacity, read normally, bind the output before its first AW
new_capability_hypothesis: Start the necessary source translation and real source read without committing to a particular output page. At a paid later binding point, use buffers that have actually become free and translations that survived the source phase. Maintain resident-free metadata from ordinary cache and ownership events rather than querying q candidate addresses for every COPY.
difference_from_round02: Round02 fixes a real destination before the existing burst_req_t first VALID; L-F requires a NEW immutable pool-parent type and an internal unbound write stage.
Round02 can only choose a slot already FREE at launch. L-F first reserves a count of FREE slots, so an eligible slot released during the source phase can later be chosen.

Round02 performs up to q ordinary-port hint queries. L-F maintains a bounded reverse index on IOTLB fill/replacement and ownership release/reservation events; selection uses that metadata and still issues the ordinary WRITE translation and permission request.

The reverse index is advisory. It stores neither PA nor reusable permission. No source PA voucher or permission replay is required when the source operation is a real READ through the unchanged IOMMU.
The small source-self-eviction example alone is fully reproduced by exact current-victim prediction or a temporary destination pin. It is not the decisive independent-benefit example.

initial_contract.immutable_public_parent: source, length, pool, context/options, epoch and tag are fixed before the NEW pool-parent VALID. That parent explicitly promises selection from a pool, not a fixed destination IOVA.
restrictions: Aligned 64-byte COPY fitting within one source 4KiB page and one destination 4KiB page; fixed destination offset 256 within each pool page for this first sketch.
Pinned, stable single-stage 4KiB mappings; one trusted pool/context per participating frontend; registered pools with matching context have disjoint virtual ranges.
Source of each active pool COPY lies outside that pool. Pool registration and normal historical warming can precede offers of FREE slots.
Application accepts any selected slot and receives its actual identity only after successful READ/WRITE/B completion and appropriate cache synchronization.

Only the first two DMA instances currently have the cited full-buffer provisioning in N mode. A four-pool state reference is a capacity design, not evidence of four native walkers or four pending source translations.

The first design supports at most the native frontend's one active parent per frontend. Ordinary controls keep all eight native AX heads, legal burst pipelining and their existing buffers; no one-child restriction is imposed on controls.

Trusted kernel serializes and validates releases exactly once; software keeps per-slot generation and leases. This same trust contract must apply to every control. Untrusted direct release and dynamic remapping require a separately priced extension.

For hand cases with one AR and one AW per64B COPY, both legal burst limits allow all8 beats; shorter configured limits require counting every additional real AR/AW/B and aggregating READ status across all children. The restricted source status callback must not treat a first R or one child completion as parent READ success.
publication_boundaries: Existing fixed-destination burst_req_t remains immutable from its first VALID and cannot implement L-F by changing dst later.
New pool-parent fields remain immutable while VALID and after acceptance. Each source AXI AR remains stable from its first VALID.
The selected destination, WRITE options and write child are frozen before their first AW VALID. There is no AW while destination is unbound.
Use a verified parent READ completion callback covering all real R beats and read status, rather than an IOTLB tag hit, first R alone, an unaccepted VALID or a snapshot tap.

state_machine.action: Check pool/context, 64B geometry and source nonoverlap; reserve completion capacity and full 64B payload capacity. Atomically require free_count > unbound_count, then increment unbound_count. Do not reserve or report a particular page yet.

Emit the ordinary source READ and normal permission checks. Collect all 8 actual R beats into charged native payload space, keeping source request fields stable. Return callback with actual parent identity and read status. No extra preparatory READ or synthetic permission is issued.

After successful real source completion, consult at most E resident metadata rows for this pool. Pick a FREE indexed slot by ordinary bounded RR; otherwise pick a FREE slot by ordinary pool RR. Atomically set chosen slot FREE->COPY and decrement both free_count and unbound_count. A stale hint cannot choose a non-FREE slot. If invalidation/config conflicts with selection, suppress hints or retry once, then ordinary free fallback.

Generate and latch the ordinary write child from the selected page and fixed offset. Run the unmodified WRITE translation/context/permissions. A stale hint may miss or fault. Publish stable AW only with a bound destination. Drain all actual W and B legally.

Only successful final B and COPY completion publish tag,pool,slot,epoch,length,status and mark consumer ownership. Completion storage was reserved before SOURCE, so it cannot block an already-issued response.

Kernel validates the software lease/generation and cache synchronization, then sends ordered trusted release. Atomically mark slot FREE, increment free_count, and update matching resident metadata. Reconfiguration requires all unbound, COPY and consumer leases to drain before changing the pool epoch.

On source fault before BIND, drain/cancel only not-yet-published work legally and release the abstract credit without output. On destination fault after binding, quarantine the slot and report error after outstanding transactions drain. Read/write error aggregation and native response draining must be designed: current NO_ERROR_HANDLING does not supply it.

credit_invariant.formula: 0 <= unbound_count <= free_count <= N; binding consumes one credit and one FREE slot atomically; a new admission requires free_count > unbound_count.
credit_invariant.purpose: Unbound source work cannot exhaust its promised output capacity. Binding may choose a newly released hot slot instead of the originally available cold slot.
credit_invariant.obligations: All allocation paths for this pool honor the same credit invariant; releases do not bypass lease validation; reconfiguration waits for credit and ownership drain. No correctness guarantee for rogue allocation/release paths is claimed.

resident_index.row: Per IOTLB way: mapped_valid1, pool2, slot6, eligible_free1 for F=4,N=64: 10 bits/way; 16 rows = 160 bits.
resident_index.fill: At a winning ordinary 4KiB non-global fill, compare the update VPN/context/stage against at most F registered ranges, derive slot by subtraction, and record that way's pool and slot with current FREE state. Normal cache tags/content still update independently; the index must not stall ordinary translation.
resident_index.replace: Overwrite the old row on actual replacement. Do not keep detached residency or count replaced data as valid.
resident_index.ownership_event: One serialized reserve/release event broadcasts (pool,slot,new_FREE) to the E small references. Only matching rows update eligibility. Concurrent fill uses resolved ownership next-state or suppresses its hint conservatively. Ordinary duplicate IOTLB entries may map to the same pool slot: reserve/release broadcasts update all matching rows, and an atomic ownership check prevents duplicate selection. Do not assume unique tags by fiat.
resident_index.invalidate: Any IOTINVAL or policy clear conservatively invalidates all index rows and beats new hints on that edge. Correctness continues through normal permission checks. No background free scan is assumed: a later fill rebuilds that row; loss of still-valid hot hints after selective invalidation is an explicit negative case.
resident_index.selection: Pool-filter and RR-reduce the E eligible bits; perform an atomic real ownership test before binding. No ordinary IOTLB hint request and no speculative PTW for unchosen pages.
resident_index.timing: The index has its own compare/reduce/mux and fanout cost. A same-cycle version may hurt Fmax; pipelined maintenance requires priced state and stale-event handling, or conservative hint drops. It is not a free extra IOTLB port.
resident_index.permissions: Exact-context range matching is conservative; skip global and non-4KiB entries in this first sketch. Normal READ and WRITE each receive their own ordinary access checks, irrespective of index eligibility.

state_reference.parameters: F=4 pools/frontends,N=64 pages/pool,E=16 actual IOTLB rows; native options O=98 bits through the current wrapper's axi_slv_id_t6.
state_reference.ownership: 4*64*2=512 bits; 00 consumer,01 COPY,10 FREE,11 quarantine. Per-slot generation32 is maintained in software, 8192 bits minimum separately, not deleted from system cost.
state_reference.parent: 4*(source64+length32+tag32+pool2+epoch32+selected_slot6+native_job_id64+FSM4+read_status2+credit_held1+options O)=956+4O bits; restricted length is validated then widened to the native64 interface.
state_reference.callback_skid: native_job_id64+frontend2+status2+valid1=69 bits; actual route/adaptation and parent association are required implementation work, not an existing callback.
state_reference.sum: 2963+4O=3355 bits at O=98; ceil/8=420 bytes of named fields only.
state_reference.two_frontend_reference: At F=2 and the corresponding pool/frontend indices reduced by one bit in both row and parent/completion formats, an exact independent worksheet is required. Do not apply the four-frontend total as measured two-DMA area.
state_reference.old_round02_actual_options: 11387+4*98=11779 bits, ceil/8=1473 bytes rather than O=32's illustrative1440.
state_reference.fair_old_trust_adjustment: Moving per-slot generation to the same trusted kernel contract also saves 8192 hardware bits for the older probe design: 3195+4O=3587 bits, ceil/8=449 bytes. Therefore the listed-field difference is only232 bits=29 bytes, not a claimed 1473->420-byte architectural saving. Layouts still differ in callback/completion contracts, so neither is net implemented area.
logic_and_unresolved: Up to F context/range compares and slot arithmetic on fill; one FREE-state mux for its resolved slot; E pool/slot comparisons for each reserve/release; pool filters, 16-way selection and address reconstruction.

Serialized ownership commands and four frontends' arbiters; register bus, CDC, status, counters, errors, callback routing, write-child regeneration, event pipelines/version state, packing/ECC and fanout costs remain separately priced.

At least64 bytes of retained source payload per active pool parent; first two N instances already have512-word buffers shared fairly with controls. Legacy three-word instances need additional capacity or explicit chunking, neither assumed free.

Existing8 AX heads,32 translated write-data words and spill/pipeline state are common resources, not eliminated or reallocated without a proof. Four index contexts do not make four translation lifecycles.
Pool memory remains4*64*4096=1MiB DDR. Kernel generation/lease tables, pinning, mapping, cache sync, consumer access, release MMIO and completion CPU traffic are additional system costs.

Equal-budget extra ordinary IOTLB entries, ports, lookahead and native concurrency remain strong controls. Powers-of-two PLRU resizing and comparator/timing costs must be included, not inferred from bit division.

index_probe_difference.scope: Stationary hand arithmetic, not a workload model or native cycles; source hit and all selected hints survive until normal write lookup; hints do not grant access.
index_probe_difference.parameters: N=64 eligible FREE pages,h=8 resident pages,q=4 uniform distinct probes,M=20 unhidden cold-endpoint delay; D=24 per64B COPY, A fixed cold destination D+M=44, E=16.
index_probe_difference.RR_expected: V=24+20*(1-8/64)=41.5; A=85.5; mean cold walks1.875 including A.
index_probe_difference.index: If all index maintenance/fanout fits the priced implementation without new serialized stall, delta_index=3 gives V=27,A=71 and1 total cold walk. Gain relative RR=14.5. Every additional maintenance/staging/consumer cost is subtracted from14.5.
index_probe_difference.strong_control: An ordinary hardware hot-first allocator with the identical complete resident-free index matches exactly. Software fresh-state allocation also matches if its full cost<=3. A cheap LIFO/page-local policy with residual miss probability p_b wins whenever20*p_b<=3+extra_cost.
index_probe_difference.boundary: This proves removal of the q-limited observation bottleneck in an explicit construction, not a novel hot-first algorithm. h=0, every FREE page resident, stale hints or cheap best-policy miss p_b=0.1 make the additional selection unhelpful.

hand_examples.source_self_eviction: Native two protected ways can hold X,Y before source S misses and fills its current victim. Early X/Y hit flags alone cannot distinguish which survives. Exact current-victim/source-miss prediction and temporary destination pin reproduce that small example; paid post-source selection is not independently superior on that example.

ownership_change.scenario: Initial resident pages Y and Z; V pool contains FREE cold X and Z currently owned by A for its pending real hot COPY Y->Z. After successful A COPY completion, Z belongs to its consumer; only after the actual consumer access/synchronization/release does it become FREE during V's necessary source S translation/read. A and V need a legal common translation-cache context/key; the default distinct PROCESS_ID values are not proof of that setup.
ownership_change.advance: V's unbound capacity credit permits starting S immediately. After Z is actually FREE and survives the source fill, V binds Z. Existing early fixed-dst COPY must choose cold X or delay its source launch until Z is released.
ownership_change.latency_condition: A's complete data transfer AND consumer release fit into the non-occupying portion of the real source translation/read critical path. This is not possible if the assumed source walk delay monopolizes the only service server.
ownership_change.strong_control: Independent source-prefetch/prepare plus waiting for Z and an ordinary late allocator may match or beat this schedule. Give it both realistic command/normal-relookup costs and a legal reusable permission-ticket implementation if it can support one; do not charge duplicate source walks by fiat.
ownership_change.quantitative_gate: For elapsed release time r, real source stage s, remaining post-source copy work w, late mechanism delta_L and source-prepare continuation delta_P: early-wait=r+s+w+delta_wait; L=max(s,r)+w+delta_L under the stated overlap; strongest prepare=max(s,r)+w+delta_P, possibly with better payload overlap. L only wins that control if its full incremental cost/area or end-to-end latency is lower. A useful region requires overlap min(s,r) to exceed overhead against wait, and a measured full-cost difference against prepare, not just the former.
ownership_change.neighbor: Release after the source stage, source walk short/fully hidden, Z evicted before binding, consumer fixed-address requirement, cheap source-prepare continuation, or zero safe buffer space removes/reverses benefit.

independent_judgments.rule: Hot-first, RR, count reservation and late pool selection are individually ordinary actions. Do not claim an independent scheduling algorithm from them.
independent_judgments.microarchitecture: Potential contribution is a demand-driven pool-parent and normal READ->late WRITE-binding contract, with event-maintained residency/ownership metadata and no extra per-copy probe/PTW or source voucher. Exact closest coverage still needs targeted verification.
independent_judgments.benefit: If a legal ownership-changing trace produces lower complete V/A cost than source preparation, pinning, current-victim prediction, layout/capacity and same-resource concurrency controls, it can supply a useful independent mechanism contribution when nearest published work does not cover that integrated capability.
independent_judgments.implementation: Design-only. New symbolic write/legalizer state, ordered release, completion and fault draining are material changes. Existing decouple_aw only delays an already-fixed AW; it does not allow rebinding.
independent_judgments.route: L-F is the next design/decisive model hypothesis. R stays backup and T stays low priority; their round02 negative conditions are not generalized beyond tested/derived cases.
independent_judgments.equivalent_implementation: The ordinary hot-first allocator with the whole same event index and pool-parent contract is an equivalent implementation, not automatically a prior published mechanism or a separate algorithm this proposal must beat. Separately attribute useful value to the index, binding point, credit and data integration through ablation; do not count the ability to copy the same proposed module into another system as proof of prior coverage.
